summary: Backend: 7/7 tests pass (root, telemetry, insights, tracking CRUD). Frontend: all requested UI flows work (4-tab bar with no AI tab, greeting 'Sasha', profile 'Sasha Giyu Bau Hasem', no Talkback/Volume/AI/mic terms, language toggle EN/ID, theme light/dark, edit-goals modal saves, goals weekly banner + bar chart + 3 goal bars, gesture simulator only has sim-double-tap and sim-long-press). CRITICAL bug found: connection state is reset to DISCONNECTED whenever user leaves the Device tab because RealBLEPanel's unmount cleanup calls onConnectChange(null) unconditionally, which flips the shared `connected` state to false. As a result: (a) after tapping device-reconnect and switching to Health, battery-bar is NOT visible and header shows OFFLINE/'Tidak Terhubung' despite the tracking pill being active; (b) attempting to stop tracking from Device after returning is ignored because toggleTracking short-circuits on !connected, so 'active-tracking-pill' stays visible. No React Native/Expo deprecated package issues detected in the tested surface.

ui_bugs.issue: Switching away from the Device tab unmounts RealBLEPanel; its cleanup calls onConnectChange(null) -> handleRealBleConnected(null) -> setConnected(false), so the app forgets the simulated (or real) connection. After tapping 'device-reconnect' and navigating to Health, battery-bar never appears and Health hero shows '--' BPM with the OFFLINE dot. Also breaks stop-tracking from the Device tab on return (toggleTracking exits early on !connected), leaving 'active-tracking-pill' stuck visible. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx lines 1289-1300 (cleanup) and 242-259 (handleRealBleConnected).

integration_issues.flow: Connect via device-reconnect -> Health tab -> stop tracking
integration_issues.issue: Connected state is lost the moment the user leaves the Device tab, which cascades into Health showing disconnected UI (no BPM number, no battery bar) and the stop-tracking control on Device becoming a no-op.

action_items: In RealBLEPanel unmount cleanup (index.tsx ~lines 1289-1300), only call onConnectChange(null) if a REAL BLE device was actually connected via this panel (guard with `if (connected)`), and even then do NOT reset the parent's demo-connected state. Recommended: give RealBLEPanel a separate 'real-only' callback, or track a `hasRealConnection` flag so the simulated/demo connection from doConnect() isn't wiped when the Device tab unmounts.

Alternative quick fix: In handleRealBleConnected, ignore null callbacks when connection was established via simulated doConnect (e.g., track a `realConnected` boolean and only setConnected(false) when the real connection was the source).

After fix, re-verify: tap device-reconnect -> switch to Health -> battery-bar visible AND greeting BPM shows a real number; then return to Device -> device-track-toggle stops tracking and active-tracking-pill disappears.
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx is 1749 lines - exceeds 700-line guideline. Should be split into per-screen modules (HealthScreen, GoalsScreen, DeviceScreen, SettingsScreen, RealBLEPanel, EditGoalsModal).
Effect cleanup in RealBLEPanel mixes real-BLE lifecycle with the shared app 'connected' state, causing tab-switch to reset the demo connection (see bug above).

rca_of_issue: RCA: RealBLEPanel is rendered only inside DeviceScreen. React unmounts it whenever `tab !== 'device'`. Its useEffect cleanup at lines 1289-1300 unconditionally calls onBpmStream(null) and onConnectChange(null). onConnectChange is `handleRealBleConnected` which, when called with null, executes `setConnected(false); setRealBpm(null);`. Reproduction: open app -> Device tab -> tap 'device-reconnect' (connected=true) -> tap 'device-track-toggle' (tracking=true) -> tap 'tab-health'. Observed: header 'OFFLINE', greeting-card without BPM, battery-bar missing. Because tracking is separate state it remains true and the tracking pill still shows, creating inconsistent UI. Mitigation: guard cleanup so it only affects the real BLE-managed connection (see action_items).
